question: Kayser-Fleischer rings — golden-brown deposits at the corneal periphery — are pathognomonic of Wilson's disease and can always be seen with the naked eye on routine examination.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Kayser-Fleischer rings require slit-lamp examination for reliable detection — they are NOT always visible to the naked eye. Furthermore, they may be absent in Wilson's disease presenting with hepatic rather than neurological features. Slit-lamp examination by an ophthalmologist is mandatory in the Wilson's workup.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct that this is FALSE. Kayser-Fleischer rings require slit-lamp examination by an ophthalmologist — they are not reliably visible to the naked eye. Additionally, they are absent in up to 50% of patients with hepatic-presenting Wilson's disease (more commonly present in neurological forms, ~95%). 'Pathognomonic when present' is more accurate than 'always present and visible without slit-lamp'.
